_podcast.theme_scoring_prompt:
Rate how well this article fits the theme 'Indigenous Lands & Innovation' — Indigenous nations using technology, governance, and stewardship on their own terms.

OUT OF SCOPE — score 0-9: geopolitical and war news with no Indigenous rights angle; general wildfire and wildlife-service updates not led by or directly affecting Indigenous communities or guardians; provincial forestry and environmental policy with no explicit First Nations involvement; consumer tech and gadget reviews; science with no Indigenous stewardship or sovereignty context; crime and judicial news unrelated to Indigenous rights.

CALIBRATION — apply this ladder to everything else. Indigenous-led journalism on governance, rights, and self-determination is a strong fit on its own: a technology hook raises a score but is NOT required to reach the top band.
- 80-100: Excellent Indigenous-led reporting. Cariboo stories bridging governance or culture AND technology land here (Tŝilhqot'in/Secwépemc/Dakelh language revitalization tech, guardian programs using sensors and drones, GIS land mapping, Indigenous-led connectivity, digital heritage projects) — and so does outstanding national coverage of sovereignty, treaty, and land rights.
- 55-79: Solid pan-Canadian Indigenous governance, sovereignty, land rights, treaty, or reconciliation journalism — APTN, Eagle Feather News, or IndigiNews-style coverage of First Nations governance, MMIWG, land claims, self-determination, and Indigenous-led services. Most Indigenous governance journalism belongs HERE, not below.
- 30-54: Indigenous cultural, community, or human-interest stories (awards, events, ceremonies) with limited governance substance, or BC land-stewardship and environmental stories with meaningful First Nations involvement.
- 10-29: General BC land, environmental, or forestry stories that mention Indigenous communities only in passing.

Nuxalk Nation leaders say the grizzly attack that killed Jennifer Balcarras and her daughter, Selah Reed, near Bella Coola has renewed trauma in a community still recovering from a separate bear attack last year. The British Columbia Conservation Officer Service said forensic evidence linked a female grizzly and her three yearling cubs to the deaths. The bears were killed, and investigators believe the attack likely involved rare predatory behaviour. Elected Chief Tlhmtimut Samuel Schooner said community support services would remain available for as long as needed. The Nuxalk Nation thanked conservation officers for resolving the incident, while saying the deaths had reopened trauma from the previous attack. Authorities also confirmed the four bears were not involved in that earlier attack, which injured 11 people.

Forecasters expected a brief lull Thursday or early Friday, followed by another strong system from Friday through Sunday. They said conditions may turn drier around Nov. 15 or 16.

items.title: [Fast Company] The UN’s climate talks are tackling this major hurdle to renewable energy
items.content_html:
🪶 ✏️

Outdated power grids are a major hurdle in the transition to renewable energy, since older systems often can’t absorb all the electricity from new, cleaner sources.

This threatens global efforts to curb climate change by reducing fossil fuels and switching to renewable energy such as solar and wind. At U.N. climate talks kicking off this week, co-hosts Turkey and Australia want more ambitious goals to slash fossil fuels, install renewables and upgrade grids.

Grid concerns are gaining urgency this year as nations race to improve their energy security following the Iran war. The U.N. recently launched a new initiative to rally funding for grid upgrades in Africa and Southeast Asia.

“There needs to be a massive, massive, massive scaling up of investments into grids if we are going to get close to meeting our climate, energy and development goals,” Selwin Hart, special adviser to the U.N. secretary-general on climate action, said.

Climate talks address grid bottleneck

At the U.N. climate talks, hosted in the Turkish resort city of Antalya, organizers describe modern and reliable electric grids as “the backbone of the clean energy system.”

But billions of dollars are needed to upgrade out-of-date grids. These steep costs could hinder further renewable energy installations.

During the U.N. General Assembly in September, the global body launched a Global Grids Accelerator to speed up international funding for electricity infrastructure in Africa and Southeast Asia.

“We’re very confident that the long-term trend is an acceleration of the pace of the energy transition, but we need the infrastructure, grids and storage, to really keep pace,” Hart said.

Annual investment in electricity generation, such as building new power plants, has risen by almost 70% since 2015, reaching $1 trillion a year, according to the International Energy Agency. Yet the agency noted annual grid spending has risen at less than half that pace.

To meet electricity demand through 2030, the IEA calculates annual grid investment must increase by about 50% from today’s $400 billion per year. Any delays will substantially increase global emissions by prolonging reliance on fossil fuels, the IEA warns.

“Power grids have not been readied enough for the scaleup of renewable electricity generation,” said Jan Rosenow, a professor of energy and climate policy at Oxford University. “We have been complacent in the past and now the grid has become a real bottleneck.”

Old grids slow energy transition

Power grids deliver electricity from power plants to homes through a network of transmission and distribution lines, substations and transformers.

Originally designed around large, centralized power plants, many of today’s power grids were built like one-way roads, with producers sending electricity to consumers. These older one-directional grids are being overwhelmed by demand surges and a boom in renewables.

Grids have a maximum capacity of electricity that they can safely store, transport and distribute. If a grid is already at capacity, solar and wind farms can be instructed to limit their electricity output, a process known as curtailment.

China and India, which have installed impressive amounts of renewables, can’t take full advantage of the massive buildout for this reason.

China curtailed 360 terawatt-hours — close to the equivalent of the United Kingdom’s annual electricity demand — of wind and solar electricity in the first half of 2026, according to Global Energy Monitor and the Center for Research on Energy and Clean Air.

India curtailed 11 terawatt-hours of solar generation — enough electricity to power about 10 million homes — over the course of 15 months spanning 2025 and 2026 because of insufficient transmission and storage capacity, according to the energy think tank Ember.

Curtailing solar and wind generation while fossil fuels continue to supply electricity is a blow to climate efforts, especially since China and India are among the world’s largest emitters, said James Abraham, with the New Delhi-based Council on Energy, Environment and Water.

To transition away from fossil fuels, he said, “you need a grid changeover. You need a grid transformation.”

Solutions exist, despite funding concerns

Upgrading existing grids to be more flexible could increase efficiency by allowing electricity flows to adjust to supply and demand. It could help areas with excess solar and wind energy send it to places with higher electricity demand and fewer energy resources.

Newer, more flexible grids could also make it easier for utility companies to exchange electricity with households that have solar panels or battery storage.

But many countries can’t afford to take these steps, or at least not quickly enough, according to Abraham, who said “the need is now. It’s a time tension rather than anything else.”

Global energy security concerns deepen

The Iran war’s energy shock built up momentum for the energy transition, especially in hard-hit regions like Southeast Asia, but investment in renewables is outpacing grid development, said Gahee Han, with the Seoul-based nonprofit Solutions for Our Climate.

“Unless we upgrade our power grid in Asia, Asia will have no choice but to rely on the conventional power plants, like gas or coal,” she said. “It’s nonsense to rely on those power plants, especially considering the energy crisis.”

One of the solutions being promoted by the Association of Southeast Asian Nations is an interconnected power grid that would allow countries to trade power more easily, adding a safeguard against future shocks.

Interest in the ambitious plan, which is still in its infancy, is growing, according to Abdul Razib Dawood, executive director of the ASEAN Center for Energy.

“We have this crisis that will unify the region. You need your neighbors,” he said. “This is an opportunity for us to really strengthen the cooperation.”

items.title: [theguardian.com] UN-backed report warns overshooting 1.5C could permanently damage Earth's ice
items.content_html:
🪶 ✏️

A report by 80 scientists convened by the International Cryosphere Climate Initiative and the U.N. Environment Programme warns that even a temporary rise above the Paris Agreement’s 1.5C warming limit could cause lasting losses to glaciers, sea ice and polar ice sheets. Earth has already warmed about 1.3C from preindustrial levels. The authors say any period above 1.5C should be as brief as possible before temperatures fall much further, and identify a long-term target below 1C by 2150. Under current policies, warming is projected to reach about 2.8C, a level the report links to near-total thaw of near-surface permafrost and likely severe disruption to ocean circulation. Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets would continue losing ice even if temperatures later returned to 1.5C, while many ice systems could take centuries or millennia to recover. The report was released ahead of the COP31 climate conference in Turkey.

items.title: [thehackernews.com] Grok Build exposes 35,578 apps, leaking sensitive company data
items.content_html:
🪶 ✏️

Security researchers found that 35,578 of 37,571 web apps built with SpaceXSI’s Grok Build, a chat-based app builder, were accessible without signing in, exposing business and personal information at SpaceXSI and 30 other organizations. Claroc, the security firm that found the apps, estimated that about one in 10 accessible apps contained internal or personal data and roughly 2% held material it rated high or critical in severity. Exposed material included a SpaceXSI sales map covering 594 strategic accounts, a hospital directory listing more than 3,500 employees, an intensive-care briefing about a patient and a timesheet with 18 users’ passwords in its code. The apps’ addresses were discoverable through searchable passive DNS records, and Grok Build preselected “Anyone with the link” as the sharing option in the researchers’ test. SpaceXSI removed 24 apps made by its own staff and X employees; Claroc said other users’ apps remained available and that it had begun contacting affected organizations.

items.content_html:
🪶 ✏️

An Italian-led research team documented repeated sexual interactions between a bull and a male donkey on an Ethiopian plateau, describing a selective social bond between the animals. During eight days of observation in March 2026, the bull, Achilles, mounted the donkey, Patroclus, 51 times; 34 mountings involved penetration. The findings appeared Nov. 2 in the journal Current Biology. The pair also licked, rubbed and nuzzled one another, and researchers repeatedly saw them seek each other out despite access to other potential mates. The team cautions that observations of one domesticated pair cannot establish why the behavior occurred or what the animals felt. Dry-season conditions led herders to move them to separate pastures; researchers in Ethiopia are trying to arrange a reunion to observe whether their interactions resume.

A review of 40 studies found that people with type 2 diabetes had a 53% higher adjusted relative risk of Alzheimer’s disease than those without diabetes. It estimated 4.7 new Alzheimer’s cases per 1,000 people with type 2 diabetes each year. A separate study of 400 adults found that two inflammation measures derived from blood counts varied across glycemic groups defined by HbA1c, but their clinical usefulness remains unestablished. Other research linked higher preoperative HbA1c to more recorded nonunion diagnoses after cervical spine fusion, while a mouse experiment found that parathyroid hormone treatments restored some diabetes-related jawbone loss. The surgery study was observational and did not establish causation or a threshold for delaying surgery; the jawbone findings have not established a treatment effect in people.

It connects AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT to Home Assistant and enables not only device control but also the creation and modification of automations, scripts, and dashboards. An optional tool search reduces the selection visible at one time to around ten tools (simon42.com, smarthomeassistent.de). Distinction: Home Assistant's own MCP integration controls only devices that are enabled for Assist. HA-MCP adds tools for configuring, creating, and repairing (simon42.com, smarthomeassistent.de).

She camped in the forest for warmth, enjoyed a campfire and clear stars, and returned safely using microspikes.
